subject: paediatrics
title: Intraventricular Haemorrhage, Leukomalacia and Patent Ductus

steps.tx: A major neurological complication in very low birth weight preterm neonates is **germinal matrix intraventricular haemorrhage**. The subependymal germinal matrix overlying the caudate nucleus is a highly vascularized embryonic zone composed of immature fragile capillaries lacking structural pericytes and smooth muscle. Impaired cerebral autoregulation leaves these vessels vulnerable to pressure fluctuations.
steps.say: Germinal matrix hemorrhage arises in fragile, gelatinous subependymal vessels in premature infants.

rows: Systemic hypertension directly transmits to capillary bed
Impaired local clot stability after microbleeds

steps.tx: Sonographic severity is classified using the **Papile intraventricular classification**. Grade one represents hemorrhage confined strictly to the subependymal germinal matrix. Grade two represents intraventricular hemorrhage filling ten to fifty percent of the lateral ventricle without ventricular dilation. Grade three exhibits extensive intraventricular blood causing acute ventricular dilatation.
steps.say: Papile grading classifies hemorrhage from germinal matrix alone to ventricular dilation and parenchymal infarction.

rows: Hemorrhage in 10 to 50% of lateral ventricle
Good, low risk of long-term disability
Intraventricular blood with acute ventricular dilation
Poor, high risk of hemiplegia and cognitive delay

steps.tx: Reading a preterm head scan means grading how far blood has travelled. In **Papile grading**, grade one blood stays in the germinal matrix, grade two enters the ventricle without stretching it, grade three dilates the ventricle, and grade four injures the surrounding white matter through venous infarction. The four panels side by side show why prognosis worsens step by step rather than gradually.
steps.say: Papile grading follows blood from the germinal matrix into the ventricle, then to dilation and white matter injury. Each grade carries a worse outlook than the one before.

vis.alt: Four panel cranial ultrasound set showing bleeding confined to the germinal matrix, then filling, dilating, and finally injuring the ventricle wall.
vis.caption: Cranial neurosonogram panels illustrating Papile grades 1 to 4 of intraventricular haemorrhage. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The most severe category, historically designated grade four, represents a **periventricular venous hemorrhagic infarction**. Rather than simple extension from the ventricle, it results from massive intraventricular blood obstructing the terminal ependymal veins, triggering venous congestion, thrombosis, and secondary ischemic necrosis in the adjacent periventricular white matter containing motor projection fibers.
steps.say: Grade four hemorrhage is a venous hemorrhagic infarction that causes permanent motor cortex damage.

left.title: Mechanism of Grade 4 Lesion
points: Venous stasis and hemorrhagic venous infarction
Destruction of descending corticospinal motor tracts

steps.tx: White matter beside the ventricles dies quietly in the sickest preterm brains. **Periventricular leukomalacia** shows first as echogenic patches on cranial ultrasound and later as small cysts in the same distribution, weeks after the insult. The corticospinal fibres to the legs run closest to the ventricles, so spastic diplegia is its commonest outcome. Serial scanning, not a single early film, is how this injury is honestly documented.
steps.say: Periventricular leukomalacia evolves from echogenic patches to cysts beside the ventricles on serial scans. It later causes spastic diplegia.

vis.alt: Cranial ultrasound parasagittal view showing periventricular leukomalacia cyst formation.
vis.caption: Small cysts are shown in white matter beside the ventricle on a parasagittal scan. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Non-hemorrhagic ischemic injury to the cerebral white matter surrounding the lateral ventricles is **periventricular leukomalacia**. Preterm cerebral white matter watershed zones are exquisitely vulnerable to systemic hypotension, hypocarbia, and maternal chorioamnionitis. Developing pre-oligodendrocytes are selectively destroyed by inflammatory cytokines and reactive oxygen species, halting central axonal myelination.
steps.say: Periventricular leukomalacia destroys pre-oligodendrocytes in white matter watershed zones.

rows: Multiple small round cystic spaces in white matter

steps.tx: Because the motor fibers destined for the lower extremities course closest to the lateral ventricles, bilateral periventricular leukomalacia causes **spastic diplegic cerebral palsy**. Affected infants demonstrate symmetrical scissoring of the lower limbs, ankle clonus, exaggerated patellar reflexes, and delayed motor milestones, while upper extremity coordination and intellect remain relatively preserved.
steps.say: Periventricular leukomalacia damages lower limb corticospinal fibers, causing spastic diplegia.

left.title: Anatomical Predilection
points: Medial fibers supply lower extremity motor control
Lateral fibers supply upper limbs and face
Watershed ischemia selectively injures medial fibers

right.title: Classic Motor Manifestations
points: Scissoring of legs due to adductor spasticity

steps.tx: Persistent left-to-right shunting through the ductus arteriosus produces a **hemodynamically significant patent ductus**. Low circulating oxygen tension and deficient muscular media in preterms impair physiological postnatal ductal closure. Significant left-to-right shunting causes pulmonary hyperperfusion, pulmonary hemorrhage, systemic hypoperfusion, and widened pulse pressures with bounding water-hammer peripheral pulses.
steps.say: Patent ductus arteriosus causes pulmonary overcirculation, systemic hypoperfusion, and bounding pulses.

rows: Rapid diastolic runoff into pulmonary bed
Palpation of radial and dorsalis pedis pulses
Auscultation at left upper sternal border

steps.tx: Pharmacological closure of a symptomatic patent ductus is achieved using **prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors**. Intravenous indomethacin or ibuprofen competitively inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes, halting production of vasodilatory prostaglandin E2 and promoting ductal constriction. Intravenous paracetamol has emerged as a safe alternative, acting on the peroxidase site of prostaglandin H2 synthase with minimal renal toxicity.
steps.say: Indomethacin, ibuprofen, or paracetamol inhibit prostaglandin synthesis to close the patent ductus.

left.title: Ibuprofen and Indomethacin
points: Risks: transient oliguria, elevated creatinine, NEC

right.title: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
points: Inhibits peroxidase catalytic site of PGHS
Significantly lower incidence of renal and gut toxicity

steps.tx: Premature infants universally experience a physiological drop in hemoglobin termed **anemia of prematurity**. Attributable to blunted hepatic and renal erythropoietin production in response to hypoxia, shortened red cell lifespan, rapid somatic growth, and iatrogenic phlebotomy blood losses, it presents as normocytic normochromic anemia. Management relies on phlebotomy reduction, oral iron supplementation, and packed red cell transfusions.
steps.say: Anemia of prematurity is a normocytic hyporegenerative anemia worsened by frequent phlebotomy.

rows: Recombinant human erythropoietin in select cases
Fetal erythrocytes survive only 60 to 70 days
Ensure adequate enteral folate and vitamin E
Rapid doubling of blood volume with growth
Elemental iron 2 to 4 mg/kg/day from 4 to 6 weeks
